rationale:
Issue #1029 reports that the formatter collapses an empty catch clause onto the same line as a following finally (`} on Exception catch (e) {} finally {`), producing misleading output. The minimized production patch touches only lib/src/source_visitor.dart: it extracts the pre-existing empty-block split rule into `_splitEmptyBlock(Block)` and adds the missing CatchClause-with-finallyBlock case, so the same invariant already applied to `if`/`else` empty then-blocks now also covers catch/finally. The helper extraction is intrinsic to the fix (same call site, same behavior for the if/else path), not an independent refactor. Critically, the minimization dropped the three unrelated changes present in the original commit: the `blockRule` null-assertion cleanup in argument_list_visitor.dart, the `final _parent` change in nesting_level.dart, the stray `@override` removal on the local `visitClause` function, and the CHANGELOG edit. The triggers are the unchanged upstream project-native fixtures from the fixing commit (test/regression/1000/1029.unit reproduces the exact snippet from the issue body; three cases appended to test/splitting/statements.stmt cover catch, `on`, and multiple catches with finally), executed through the existing test/formatter_test.dart harness; they depend only on the public formatter entry point, not on any API introduced by the fix. Strict evidence for both the original and post-minimization revisions passes every gate (build both versions, buggy differential with both selectors reproduced, fixed isolated/suite/reversed clean, full suite green on fixed, 3 repetitions, deterministic fingerprints). active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so #1029 is not a duplicate, and it matches allowed_root_cause_ids.

Issue #1029 ('Formatting of empty catch blocks can appear misleading') reports that dart_style collapses an empty catch body onto the same line as a following `finally`, producing `} on Exception catch (e) {} finally {`. The minimized production patch touches only lib/src/source_visitor.dart: it moves the pre-existing empty-block split condition into a new private helper `_splitEmptyBlock(Block)` and adds the missing case where the empty block is a CatchClause body of a TryStatement that has a finallyBlock. That is exactly the reported behavior gap in the pre-existing empty-block handling path, not a new capability layered on top of unrelated work. The two unrelated null-safety/style cleanups present in the original commit (argument_list_visitor.dart `Rule? get blockRule` -> `Rule get blockRule`, nesting_level.dart `_parent` made final, and the stray `@override` removal on the local `visitClause` function) are excluded from patches/minimized-production.patch, so the minimized patch is behavior-only for this defect; no CHANGELOG or config change is included. The trigger is upstream project-native fixture data from the same fixing commit: test/regression/1000/1029.unit reproduces the issue's exact snippet, and the three added cases in test/splitting/statements.stmt cover `catch (err) {} finally`, `on Exception {} finally`, and multiple empty catches with a finally — all the same root cause, all driven through the existing test/formatter_test.dart harness, with no dependency on any API introduced by the fix (`_splitEmptyBlock` is private and never referenced by the fixtures). Machine-generated strict gates pass both pre- and post-minimization: build on both revisions, unique selectors (2/2), buggy differential reproducing both declared selectors, deterministic fingerprints (4/4 groups), fixed isolated/suite/reversed runs clean, and buggy full suite failing only on the reproduced triggers. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and dart-lang/dart_style#1029 is the single allowed verified issue key, so this root cause is not a duplicate.
